text:
raj: Hey team — BigBank asked during the POC kickoff: what exact evidence/retention windows we can provide for ISO 27001 audits? They want mapping to our ISMS policies and how retention ties to data classification + KMS ownership. Can we get a short answer for SOW + pricing call tomorrow?
jess: quick / high-level: we provide audit logs (read/write/role changes), config snapshots, and access reviews. Default retention: 90 days for detailed logs, 1 year for aggregated metrics, 7 years for formal compliance artifacts (pdf exports). We can negotiate for enterprise customers.
raj: do we have this in a one-pager I can share?
liz: yes — see https://redwood.internal/docs/iso/evidence-retention (internal). But for the POC we should boil it down: 90d logs, 1y metrics, KMS key rotation history kept for 7y.
sam: BigBank specifically asked about data classification — e.g., if a dataset is classified "restricted", do we hold full request/response text for 90 days? or redacted?
jess: good q. Policy says: for "restricted" class we store request metadata + hashed identifiers for 90 days. Full plaintext conversation only retained if customer opts in and signs DPA addendum for POC. Otherwise we redact PII and only store token counts and embeddings.
marco: any impact on pricing if they opt-in to full retention?
jess: yes — storing full conversation text increases storage + legal review. For POC we add a small flat fee (one-time) to cover retention & KMS usage. Also, if they want >90 days for full text, that's a recurring storage charge. I can put numbers in an email.
raj: can you drop the exact wording I should use in the SOW? short copy please.
jess: copy to paste: "Redwood will provide the following compliance evidence during the POC: system audit logs (90 days), aggregated service metrics (1 year), and compliance artifact exports (7 years). For data labelled 'restricted', Redwood retains request metadata and non-reversible hashed identifiers for 90 days by default. Full plaintext retention for restricted data is only available with an explicit customer addendum and will incur additional storage and encryption key management fees."
raj: perfect. include KMS ownership sentence?
jess: add: "Customer-managed KMS can be configured for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted POC Redwood manages KMS by default. When customer-managed KMS is used, key rotation logs and key-lifecycle evidence will be provided as part of the compliance package."
raj: thanks. one last ask — BigBank's security team asked for the ISO control mapping (e.g., A.8, A.12) that these artifacts satisfy. Do we have a quick mapping?
liz: short mapping: A.8 (asset management) -> data classification + retention; A.9 (access control) -> audit logs + access reviews; A.12 (ops) -> config snapshots & change logs; A.10 (cryptography) -> KMS usage and key rotation records; A.16 (incident mgmt) -> incident timelines and postmortems.
marco: add note that this is implementation-level evidence; they may ask for policy docs too (ISMS policies, Acceptable Use, Encryption policy).
raj: can someone attach the policy doc (pdf) to the thread so I can forward?
security-bot: Document uploaded: /internal/isos/ISMS_Policy_v2.3.pdf (access: redwood-team).
raj: got it, forwarding now. i'll also mention the extra fee if they want full retention beyond default. thanks all :thumbsup:
jess: np. tagging @sales-eng for numbers; i'll follow up with a short pricing table and a snippet to paste into the SOW by EOD.
sam: thx — i'll prep the customer-facing one-pager with the key bullets and the mapping to ISO controls.
raj: excellent. closing the loop after pricing lands.
